summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a long history of mast cell activation syndrome was admitted for a typical flare characterized by chest pain, wheezing, dyspnea, and diffuse discomfort. She presented to the emergency department after symptoms became intolerable, with no identifiable trigger. Initial evaluation, including chest X-ray and EKG, showed no acute cardiopulmonary issues, and labs were within normal limits. She was treated with her established IV regimen of Benadryl, Dilaudid, and Ativan every four hours, with gradual improvement in symptoms. An ipratropium inhaler was added to manage wheezing, as she preferred to avoid albuterol due to anxiety. Her other conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, orthostatic hypotension, and mood disorders, remained stable, with home medications continued. She expressed emotional distress about the chronic nature of her illness and was encouraged to follow up with her primary doctor, rheumatologist, and a psychiatrist. By discharge, she was ambulatory, breathing comfortably, and able to manage symptoms on oral medications.
